pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered around customisation and progression rather than beginner framing, which was correctly pitched at a six-year practitioner — 'we're going to look at sticking points, we're going to look at, you know, where we're weak, where we want to get stronger. And Trevor's actually mapping out a custom program to you that's updated every single week.' The prospect volunteered the strongest reaction of the call: 'that's exactly, that's, that sounds exactly what I'm looking for, without even having known exactly. So that's what, you know, your guys' focus was.' Worth noting that the mobility half of the pillar was delivered generically as injury prevention for ageing, and never touched the specific shoulder mobility restriction the prospect had described fifteen minutes earlier as one of his two goals.

The weakest of the three deliveries and correspondingly the flattest reaction. Pitched around adding muscle mass and sustainability — 'you mentioned how it'd be nice to put on a little bit more muscle mass. Well, great. What do we need to do?... what do we need to do to get it elite?' The prospect gave a single line of agreement with no elaboration, no question and no tie to his own situation: 'I... I think that's exactly right up my alley.' He had already said his weight is stable at 180 to 182, that he does not count protein but focuses on it, and that physique is explicitly not his reason for buying, so this pillar had comparatively little to attach to.

Delivered with the download-Trevor's-brain framing and the teach-to-fish exit. The prospect responded by comparing it favourably to his existing coaching relationships and naming the differentiator himself: 'I love it. You know, look, I've done this before with other coaches that I'm still really close to, but, you know, it seems that Trevor is so much more focused on kettlebells, I happen to be also, and so that's what's, you know, sort of drawn me to you guys.' That is a prospect articulating the positioning better than the pitch did, and it is the single most useful sentence on the call for marketing: specialisation is what moves this buyer, not coaching quality, which he already has access to.

anchors.raw: he puts up enough variety that, again, I could just draft off of him and pick and choose and, you know, forever. And maybe that's what we'll end up doing.
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free Instagram and TikTok content
anchors.note: The most consequential anchor in this batch. The competitor against $6,000 is not another coach, it is the company's own marketing, and the prospect has been running on it successfully for years — saving workouts, choosing push or pull days, adopting the loaded-carry walks to Central Park. He states plainly that continuing forever is a real option. Unusually, the counterweight was also supplied by the prospect: he volunteered guilt about it twice, including 'I sort of feel guilty that I'm sort of like taking Trevor's work for free' and 'it is true. I feel guilty that I've been, you know, following him so religiously.' Neither the anchor nor its antidote was touched by the rep.

anchors.raw: I guess I pay for another app called Ladder, and there's a, you know, I follow one of the kettlebell instructors on Ladder... the Ladder workouts are almost like too easy for me, and I feel like I'm not getting challenged
anchors.competitor: Ladder (coach Lauren Kansky), approximately $100 per month
anchors.note: A $100-a-month kettlebell subscription against $1,000 a month, a sixtyfold-per-month difference the rep never framed. The good news is that the prospect had already disqualified it himself on the only axis that matters to him — challenge — which is the strongest possible position to sell from. The rep did investigate the contract terms and established it was month-to-month and cancellable at will, which correctly removed it as a blocker, but never used the too-easy admission as a price justification.

anchors.raw: The guy who owns this gym in New York, who I, you know, up until now have said this is the smartest guy that I've met in fitness, and he is, his name is Kelvin Gary, he was a college football player, he was a college tight end at University of Miami, and he's become a dear friend, and I've done this all with him.
anchors.competitor: Kelvin Gary, New York gym owner
anchors.note: He already buys high-end one-to-one coaching, trains with Gary three or four times a month, and used him as the benchmark when rating Primal a 10. Crucially he also said he stopped progressing with him — 'I stopped, because I felt like I got everything I could get from him' — which is the same reason he is leaving Ladder. This anchor supports the price because it establishes he pays for elite coaching as a matter of course, and it establishes the churn pattern the rep should have named: this prospect leaves coaches when he stops progressing, which makes the guarantee the most relevant asset in the offer.

anchors.raw: And I guess the other issue is that I probably do, will need to invest in some heavier kettlebells than what I've got. So I guess I've got to think about that, too, as I progress.
anchors.note: Raised by the prospect at the exact moment he was declining to pay, and answered with 'I mean, which is good.' It adds an unquantified cost on top of the $6,000 for his New York location, where he has lighter bells than at the Long Island house. Minor in absolute terms for this buyer, but it is a real addition to total cost that surfaced during the close and was waved away rather than priced or absorbed.

unmet_demand.want: Shoulder mobility work specific enough to unlock windmills and progress the Turkish get-up past 12 to 14 kg per arm. He named it as one of only two goals when asked directly: 'I have trouble with the windmills, I guess shoulder mobility would be great... because of my shoulder mobility, maybe it's just too much focus on some of the pushups and not getting my shoulders.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never referenced again. The mobility half of the training pillar was delivered as generic ageing and injury prevention — 'we want to actually add in the mobility so that we can have the longevity' — with nothing about assessing or correcting an overhead restriction. The programme almost certainly does exactly this, and it is also the most plausible cause of the overhead plateau he is paying to fix, so the connection was available and free.

unmet_demand.want: A credible route to 26 kg doubles overhead in six months, the specific and only numeric target he set.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered by assertion — 'by the end of this, we absolutely expect to see massive increases in your strength, massive increases in your lifts' — with no mention of how overhead pressing is periodised, what a realistic six-month jump from 22 to 24 kg actually looks like, or why his current self-programming has stalled. The performance guarantee read out later does cover press progression at eight kilograms across three of five lifts, which is materially relevant to his exact goal, and the rep did not connect it to the goal when he read it.

unmet_demand.want: Training that survives frequent travel. He volunteered that travel breaks his routine and that hotel gyms do not motivate him: 'If I'm traveling for work or I'm traveling for, with my family and I don't get to work out, I sort of feel, like, negative' and 'even when I go, when I'm traveling and there's a gym, then it's hard for me to sort of, like, motivate myself.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not addressed at all. This is the second prospect in this batch to raise travel as the structural threat to consistency and the second time it went unanswered. That it recurs across different prospects with the same rep suggests a missing standard answer rather than an individual oversight.

unmet_demand.want: Written terms before payment. He asked for them at the point of collection — 'I would love to see something a little bit more in writing before I give you my credit card' — and then wanted to read them before committing.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Served on the call, and served well: the rep shared his screen and read the entire agreement aloud including the guarantee and its eligibility conditions. Recorded here because the process has no pre-read step, and for a buyer of this type — a former head of M&A who reads contracts for a living — the absence of documentation before the card request is what converted a 10-out-of-10 call into a deferral. The material itself was strong enough to close on and simply arrived after the ask.
